words.note: An easy, everyday greeting.
An informal question used with someone you know.
A useful polite expression.
Say this when parting.
Your home; masculine noun.
A feminine noun.
Also خونه (khuna) in everyday usage.
Present forms: خلاصوي (he/she opens), خلاصوم (I open), خلاصوې (you open).
Masculine adjective; describes کور.
S–O–V: هغه (subject) • دروازه (object) • خلاصوي (verb).
Masculine کور takes لوی and دی. The English “it” is part of the meaning; Pashto does not need an extra “it”.
Treated as feminine plural when describing it.
Masculine noun.
څښي = he/she drinks; څښم = I drink; څښې = you drink.
Masculine form; سړې when describing اوبه.
S–O–V: هغه • اوبه • څښي.
اوبه behaves like a plural noun, so we say سړې دي.
Place to buy and sell.
Can mean bread, food, or a meal.
A small shop or store.
خوري = he/she eats; خورم = I eat; خورې = you eat.
Describes bread, fruit, or other food.
S–O–V: هغه • ډوډۍ • خوري.
Feminine ډوډۍ uses ده.
A masculine noun.
Also مکتب (maktab) in some Afghan families.
لولي = he/she reads; لولم = I read; لولې = you read.
Masculine form for a new book.
S–O–V: هغه • کتاب • لولي.
Masculine کتاب uses دی.
Another familiar part of a home.
زه په کور کې اوسېږم = I live in the house.
Masculine form; کوچنۍ for a feminine noun.
په ... کې indicates in; اوسېږم carries first-person singular.
An old verb + a new noun; first-person singular ends in ـم.
کوچنی changes to کوچنۍ for the feminine noun کوټه.
A fish you might see in the river.
وینم = I see; وینې = you see; ویني = he/she sees.
Masculine پاک; feminine پاکه, as in کوټه پاکه ده.
Saleha notices a fish. Earlier you learned هغه (he/she); now زه and وینم mean “I see”.
Compare Day 2: هغه اوبه څښي (he/she drinks water) with زه اوبه څښم (I drink water). The ending tells you who does it.
پاکې agrees with feminine-plural اوبه.
A feminine noun.
اخلم = I buy; اخلې = you buy; اخلي = he/she buys.
ګرانه with feminine مڼه.
زه + مڼه + اخلم: I + apple + buy. Pashto action verbs generally follow the object.
Notice خوري (he/she eats) → خورم (I eat).
ګرانه agrees with the feminine noun مڼه.
A writing instrument.
لیکم = I write; لیکې = you write; لیکي = he/she writes.
Can describe a lesson or book.
په ... کې means “in”; لیکم is first person.
Previously: هغه کتاب لولي. Now: زه کتاب لولم.
New adjective, familiar noun.
A piece of furniture.
پاکوې = you clean; پاکوم = I clean.
Masculine form; describes مېز.
ته is informal singular “you”; پاکوې is second-person singular.
Same door and opening verb as earlier, changed person.
This descriptive sentence reuses the table.
A small body of standing water.
لامبو وهې = you swim; لامبو وهم = I swim.
Masculine adjective describing pond or river.

words.ps: ته په ډنډ کې لامبو وهې.
words.roman: ta pa ḍanḍ ke laambo wahe
words.note: په ... کې = in, and لامبو وهې is the second-person form.
څښي → څښم → څښې across the first three loops.
A descriptive sentence with a new adjective.
The money you pay at a market.
ورکوې = you give; ورکوم = I give.
ارزانه with the feminine noun ډوډۍ.
ته + پیسې + ورکوې.
اخلم changes to اخلې with ته.
ارزانه describes feminine ډوډۍ.
The material learned at school.
زده کوې means “you learn”.
Used to describe a lesson.
زده کول forms the expression زده کوې.
The same familiar book; a second-person verb.
Adjective ښه describing درس.
People belonging to a family.
خبرې کوو = we talk; خبرې کوې = you talk.
Can describe a person or family.

words.ps: موږ په کور کې خبرې کوو.
words.roman: moong pa kor ke khabare kawoo
words.note: موږ is we; present first-person plural often ends in ـو.
Reuse اوسېدل, now first-person plural.
A familiar drink.
ځو = we go; ځم = I go; ځې = you go.
Often used for a hot drink.
څښل changes to څښو with موږ.
ته after a destination can mean “to”.
Tea is treated as masculine here.
A generic word for fruit.
پلورو = we sell; پلورئ = you sell.
خوږه can describe feminine مېوه.
اخلم → اخلو with موږ.
New market verb پلورل.
The masculine adjective خوږ becomes feminine خوږه.
The language you are learning.
Masculine form for a student.
Opposite of اسانه (easy).
The verb form changes with موږ.
لولي → لولم → لولې → لولو.
New adjective + remembered noun.
A visitor at home.
Used for an unlit room.
تاسې is polite or plural “you”; ـئ is a frequent present ending.
Reuses لیدل and introduces formal/plural conjugation.
A familiar noun with a new adjective.
Water falling from the sky.
Used here for calm water.
څښو → څښئ contrasts we and you plural.
ته after سیند indicates movement towards the river.
A descriptive present-tense sentence.
A common market purchase.
Can describe cooked food or ripe fruit, depending on context.
Reuses اخیستل with a plural/polite second-person ending.
The same verb from the “we” loop changes ending.
پخه agrees with feminine ډوډۍ.
A small writing book.
Used here to describe a masculine book.
Different form from informal ته کتاب لولې.
Reuses لیکل and په ... کې.
New adjective + old noun.
Plural noun.
لوبې کوي = he/she/they play(s).
Can describe a high sound; this round uses the verb “talk”.

words.ps: هغوی په کور کې لوبې کوي.
words.roman: haghoi pa kor ke lobe kawee
words.note: هغوی = they; کوي is the third-person form of کول.
The third-person plural verb form matches the singular for this verb.
Plural of bird.
Can describe water, light or a clear view.
هغوی is plural, but څښي resembles the singular third-person form.
Reuses the verb تلل, now third-person plural.
New adjective + old noun.
Plural collective word.
خوښوي = he/she/they like(s).
Quantifier whose form depends on the noun.
Third-person plural present tense.
Reuses مېوه with a new verb.
Plural of کتاب.
Often applied to work or lessons.
Old verb, new plural noun.
Same action you learned with ته and موږ.
Review درس and add a new adjective.
Masculine خلاص; feminine خلاصه, as in دروازه خلاصه ده.
شین can cover blue and green depending on context and speaker. Here we use it for the river.
words.dialect: The colour term شین varies between blue and green by context; verify local usage.

words.note: Door is feminine, so the adjective has ـه and “is” is ده.
Room is feminine: پاکه ده.
River is masculine: شین دی. شین can also refer to green.
Market is masculine: لوی دی.
Shop is masculine, so we use خلاص دی.
School is masculine, so we use لوی دی.
A bird you might see near the water.
زه ګرځم = I walk around / stroll. The present stem changes, so verb forms are learned as complete words.
زه کېنم = I sit. Notice the first-person verb form, not merely an added ending.
A written or spoken word.
A common market vegetable; کچالو may refer to one potato or potatoes by context.
Onions for tonight’s meal.
A shopping bag for carrying groceries.
زه غواړم = I want. This is an irregular-looking present stem: learn غواړم as a whole.
زه وړم = I carry / take. Compare the third-person form وړي.
Reuses وینم (I see) with a new noun.

words.ps: زه د سیند پر غاړه کېنم.
words.roman: za da seend par ghāṛa kenam
words.note: د سیند پر غاړه = on the riverbank; کېنم expresses “I sit”.

words.ps: زه د سیند پر غاړه ګرځم.
words.roman: za da seend par ghāṛa garzam
words.note: A new action with a familiar location; ګرځم = I stroll/walk around.
Day 2 had هغه دروازه خلاصوي. Now change the verb ending to describe your own action.

words.ps: زه په کور کې کتاب لولم.
words.roman: za pa kor ke kitaab lolum
words.en: I read a book at home.
words.note: Reuses the Day 2 verb “read” and Day 1 “house”, now from the first-person point of view.

words.ps: زه په کور کې اوبه څښم.
words.roman: za pa kor ke oba ts-khum
words.note: Practise the familiar verb “drink” with the home location.
A new classroom noun plus the familiar verb لیکم (I write).
Open is familiar from Day 2, but its object is now a book.
New adjective نوی from Day 1, and I read لولم from Day 3.
Reuse اخلم (I buy) with a new vegetable.
The verb غواړم expresses first-person wanting. An appropriate request at the grocer.
Practise the first-person verb وړم with shopping vocabulary.
Combine Day 1 bread with the Day 3 verb for buying.
بندوي = he/she closes. Useful for closing a book at school or the door at home.
خرڅوي = he/she sells. Edris sells food to customers at his shop.
A common item to buy at the market. شیدې is grammatically plural.
غورځوي = he/she throws. At the lake, someone throws a stone into the water.
نیسي = he/she catches or holds. Beside the lake, someone catches a fish.
A stone beside the river or lake.
A familiar drink when visiting Muhammad Jan at home.
پاکوي = he/she cleans. Compare the Day 1 adjective پاک (clean).
In the classroom, a student writes a word. هغه (subject) + کلمه (object) + لیکي (verb). Day 3 changes لیکي to لیکم (I write).
A familiar action from the house, now used with a classroom book. The verb still comes last.
Ms Hameed shows the opposite of opening a book. بندوي means he/she closes.
The adjective نوی is from Day 1, and لولي is from today. The object phrase نوی کتاب precedes the verb.
At Edris’s shop, a customer buys an apple. Day 3 will change اخلي to اخلم (I buy).
Edris sells bread at the market. Revisit the Day 1 noun ډوډۍ with a new action verb.
A shopper carries a bag away from the market. Day 3 lets you say زه کڅوړه وړم (I carry a bag).
Another purchase from Edris. The market verb اخلي stays at the end of the sentence.
Saleha points out a fish at the lake. Day 3: زه کب وینم (I see a fish).
Reuse the verb ویني with a different lake animal. The bird will return on Day 3.
A person throws a stone beside the river. A human subject can perform this action; a door cannot.
Another plausible lake activity. The fish is the object, and نیسي (catches) ends the sentence.
Muhammad Jan compares opening the door (خلاصوي) with closing it (بندوي).
A familiar home activity, using the verb څښي learned at the lake and the new noun چای.
Day 1 described a clean room (کوټه پاکه ده). Day 2 describes someone cleaning that room (پاکوي).
Reuse خلاصوي from the door with a different object. Day 3: زه کړکۍ خلاصوم (I open the window).
A chair inside the house.
A basket used for groceries.
A question asked in class.
A complete sentence.
Muhammad Jan revisits the familiar room from Day 1 and contrasts ـې with first-person ـم.
A first-person action in the house; the ending identifies “I”.

words.ps: ته چای څښې او زه اوبه څښم.
words.roman: ta chaay tshey aw za oba tshkam
words.en: You drink tea, and I drink water.
words.note: Two natural clauses with different subjects and verb endings, joined by او.

words.ps: ته کوټه پاکوې او زه پر څوکۍ کښېنم.
words.roman: ta kota paakawey aw za par tsokey kenam
words.en: You clean the room, and I sit on the chair.
words.note: An informal address to a peer is quoted for practice; Muhammad Jan is not being addressed as ته.

words.ps: ته کړکۍ خلاصوې او زه کوټه پاکوم.
words.roman: ta karkay khlaasawey aw za kota paakawum
words.en: You open the window, and I clean the room.
words.note: Reuse window and clean with an informal second-person and a first-person clause.
The action suits a customer at Edris’s market.
A common market activity.

words.ps: ته مڼې اخلې او زه کڅوړه وړم.
words.roman: ta manay akhley aw za katswara wrum
words.en: You buy apples, and I carry a bag.
words.note: Two shoppers do different things.

words.ps: ته ډوډۍ اخلې او زه مڼې اخلم.
words.roman: ta dodai akhley aw za manay akhlam
words.en: You buy bread, and I buy apples.
words.note: Two shoppers buy different produce.
Saleha points to fish by the lake.

words.ps: ته مرغۍ وینې او زه کب وینم.
words.roman: ta marghay weeney aw za kab weenam
words.en: You see a bird, and I see a fish.
words.note: Two friends notice different animals at the lake.

words.ps: ته اوبه څښې او زه کب وینم.
words.roman: ta oba tshey aw za kab weenam
words.en: You drink water, and I see a fish.
words.note: The two actions naturally occur at the lake.
New classroom noun with the informal second-person ending.

words.ps: ته کتاب لولې او زه کلمه لیکم.
words.roman: ta kitaab loley aw za kalima leekam
words.en: You read a book, and I write a word.
words.note: Classmates work on different tasks.

words.ps: ته درس زده کوې او زه کتاب لولم.
words.roman: ta dars zda kawey aw za kitaab lolam
words.en: You learn a lesson, and I read a book.
words.note: Two complementary classroom activities.
A normal classroom response, with the informal pronoun used between peers.
Respectfully addressing Muhammad Jan.
An elder opening a house door.

words.ps: تاسې چای څښئ او زه اوبه څښم.
words.roman: taase chaay tshkey aw za oba tshkam
words.en: You drink tea, and I drink water. (polite)
words.note: One clause politely addresses an elder, the next uses “I”.
A respectful conversation about reading at home.
Respectfully addressing Edris at his grocery store.
Edris sells fresh fruit at his market stall.
Can address more than one shopper or a single respected customer.

words.ps: تاسې سبزي اخلئ او زه ډوډۍ اخلم.
words.roman: taase sabzee akhley aw za dodai akhlam
words.en: You buy vegetables, and I buy bread. (plural)
words.note: Speaking to a group of shoppers.
Talking to a group beside the lake.

words.ps: تاسې مرغۍ وینئ او زه کب وینم.
words.roman: taase marghay weeney aw za kab weenam
words.en: You see a bird, and I see a fish. (plural)
words.note: At the gathering, the villagers see different animals.

words.ps: تاسې اوبه څښئ او زه چای څښم.
words.roman: taase oba tshkey aw za chaay tshkam
words.en: You drink water, and I drink tea. (plural)
words.note: Drinks shared at the community gathering.
Ms Hameed addresses the class together.
The teacher addresses the class collectively.

words.ps: تاسې کتاب لولئ او زه کلمه لیکم.
words.roman: taase kitaab loley aw za kalima leekam
words.en: You read a book, and I write a word. (polite/plural)
words.note: The class and the teacher work on different tasks.

loops.label: It / Things
loops.subtitle: Simple descriptions · no action verbs yet
loops.description: Begin by naming things. Describe a door, river, market and book using easy present-tense “is” sentences. The village teachers explain masculine, feminine and plural endings.

loops.label: He / She
loops.subtitle: Third-person singular · present tense · action sentences
loops.description: Begin at school with Ms Hameed to learn Pashto S–O–V order, then practise at the market and lake before finishing at home.

loops.label: I
loops.subtitle: First-person singular · present-tense verb endings · shopping for dinner
loops.description: Meet Saleha at the lake first to learn how زه (I) changes present-tense verbs. Practise with Muhammad Jan, Ms Hameed and Edris, then return to Edris to shop for dinner in your final conversation.

loops.label: You (informal)
loops.subtitle: Informal singular you · verb endings · compound sentences
loops.description: Start at home with Muhammad Jan. Learn to change “I” into informal “you” (ته) and join two clauses with او (and). Practise at market, lake and school; finish with an informal conversation with Muhammad Jan.

loops.label: You (polite/plural)
loops.subtitle: Respectful singular and plural you · choosing your audience
loops.description: Begin at school with Ms Hameed, who teaches when to use ته and تاسې and how verbs change. Meet villagers across the town, then join a lakeside gathering where you must address people appropriately.

loops.label: We
loops.subtitle: First-person plural · present tense
loops.description: Speak as a group, with new words and plural-present verb endings. Villagers may now appear away from their usual home bases.

loops.label: They
loops.subtitle: Third-person plural · present tense
loops.description: Describe what groups of people do, combining the whole vocabulary bank.

residential.name: Your Home
residential.intro: Doors, rooms, family and everyday actions.
